ideas.title: Add AI Cache Analytics Hook
ideas.description: Create a useAICacheMetrics hook that exposes AI cache statistics including hit rate, miss rate, fuzzy match rate, and total cached prompts. This enables users to understand cache effectiveness and optimize their prompt usage patterns.
ideas.rationale: The codebase has established metrics hook patterns (useModelMetrics, useErrorMetrics) that aggregate localStorage data and expose stats via useMemo. The aiCache service already tracks exact and fuzzy matches but lacks a corresponding analytics hook to surface this data to users.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add cache hit/miss tracking to aiCache.get() and getSimilar() methods by storing access records. 2. Dispatch 'ai-cache-access' event on each access. 3. Create useAICacheMetrics hook following useModelMetrics structure with stats like hitRate, missRate, fuzzyHitRate, totalCached, cacheUsageBytes. 4. Wire to PerformanceMetricsPanel for display.

ideas.title: Extend Error Handler for AI Provider-Specific Errors
ideas.description: Enhance the error classification system to recognize and provide user-friendly messages for AI provider-specific errors including Gemini quota exceeded, Replicate model cold start/warming, OpenRouter credit exhaustion, and API-specific rate limits.
ideas.rationale: The errorHandler.ts already classifies generic network errors (timeout, CORS, 429 rate limit) but doesn't distinguish between AI providers. Since the app uses Gemini, OpenRouter, and Replicate, provider-specific error messages would help users troubleshoot issues faster.
existing_patterns: Provider-specific error handling in service files
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add new error types to NetworkError.type union: 'gemini_quota' | 'replicate_warmup' | 'openrouter_credits'. 2. Extend classifyError() with provider-specific message patterns (e.g., 'billing not enabled', 'model is warming up', 'insufficient credits'). 3. Update user-friendly messages with actionable guidance. 4. Consider adding provider detection from error response headers/body.

ideas.title: Add Snapshot Favorites and Search
ideas.description: Extend useCanvasSnapshots hook with favorites toggle and search functionality, following the established usePromptHistory pattern. This allows users to mark important snapshots and quickly find them by name.
ideas.rationale: usePromptHistory has a mature pattern with toggleFavorite(), searchPrompts(), and getFavoritePrompts() methods. useCanvasSnapshots currently only supports CRUD operations without favorites or search, despite having a similar data structure (records with id, name, timestamps).
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add isFavorite field to SnapshotRecord interface. 2. Implement toggleFavorite(id) following usePromptHistory pattern. 3. Add searchSnapshots(query) that searches name field. 4. Add getFavoriteSnapshots() sorted by updatedAt. 5. Update SnapshotsModal UI with star icon for favorites and search input.

ideas.title: Add Compare Models Voice Command
ideas.description: Expose the existing compareModelPerformance() function as a voice command that allows users to verbally request model comparisons and receive spoken recommendations based on speed, quality, or cost criteria.
ideas.rationale: The modelRouter.ts already implements sophisticated model comparison with compareModelPerformance() that ranks models by criteria. The Command pattern in services/commands/ enables adding new voice commands. Currently no voice command surfaces this capability despite it being useful for hands-free workflow optimization.
existing_patterns: Command class with name and execute(args, context)
Voice command tool definitions in actionExecutor
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create CompareModelsCommand class implementing Command interface. 2. Accept args: { capability: string, criteria: 'speed'|'quality'|'cost'|'balanced' }. 3. Call filterModelsByCapability() then compareModelPerformance(). 4. Return formatted result string listing top 3 models with scores and reasons. 5. Register command in actionExecutor AVAILABLE_TOOLS. 6. Add voice tool definition for OpenAI Realtime API.

ideas.title: Add Storage Usage Dashboard Component
ideas.description: Create a StorageUsagePanel component that visualizes localStorage usage across all StorageManager namespaces, showing per-namespace usage, total usage, and quota remaining with a progress bar.
ideas.rationale: StorageManager.getUsage() already returns character count per namespace, and the codebase has 7 storage namespaces (aiCache, errorMetrics, modelPreferences, modelMetrics, onboarding, promptHistory, snapshots). No UI currently exposes this to users, but storage quota is a real concern especially with canvas snapshots storing base64 images.
existing_patterns: Progress bar styling from existing UI components
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Export a getGlobalStorageStats() function from storageManager.ts that iterates all namespace instances and calls getUsage(). 2. Create StorageUsagePanel.tsx component with progress bars per namespace. 3. Show total usage vs estimated quota (5MB typical). 4. Add clear buttons per namespace calling storage.clear(). 5. Integrate into SettingsModal under a 'Storage' tab or accordion section.

ideas.title: Add Password Visibility Toggle to AuthModal
ideas.description: Add a show/hide password toggle button to the password input field in the authentication modal, allowing users to verify their password entry before submission.
ideas.rationale: Password visibility toggles are a standard UX pattern that reduce login friction and prevent errors. Currently users must type passwords blindly, which can lead to typos and failed login attempts especially on mobile devices.
ideas.current_state: The password input field uses type='password' (line 348) without any visibility toggle. Users cannot see what they've typed, making it difficult to verify input accuracy. The input has icons for validation states but no visibility toggle.
ideas.proposed_change: Add showPassword state boolean. Create an eye/eye-off icon button inside the password input field (similar to the username validation indicator pattern at lines 295-311). Toggle between type='password' and type='text' on click. Use Material Icons 'visibility' and 'visibility_off' icons. Position at right-4 with -translate-y-1/2 styling like existing icons.
ideas.user_benefit: Users can verify their password entry before submission, reducing failed login attempts and frustration, especially on mobile where typing is more error-prone.

ideas.title: Add Visible Previous Button to OnboardingTour
ideas.description: Add a visible 'Previous' button to the onboarding tour component allowing users to navigate backwards through tour steps without relying on keyboard shortcuts.
ideas.rationale: While ArrowLeft keyboard navigation exists, there's no visible Previous button. Users may miss information or want to review previous steps. Most users won't discover keyboard shortcuts without visible affordance.
ideas.current_state: The tour has Next/Finish and Skip buttons (lines 209-211, 268-286). ArrowLeft keyboard shortcut works (lines 113-115) but there's no visible Previous button. Users can only go forward visually or skip entirely.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a Previous button next to Skip when currentStep > 0. Use text-xs font-bold text-zinc-500 hover:text-white uppercase tracking-wider styling like the Skip button. Add Material Icon 'arrow_back' before the text. On click: setCurrentStep(c => c - 1). Place it in the button group at lines 208-214 (spotlight mode) and 268-275 (centered mode).
ideas.user_benefit: Users can easily review previous tour steps without needing to restart the entire tour or know keyboard shortcuts, making onboarding more user-friendly.

ideas.title: Add Voice Status Text Label During Connection States
ideas.description: Add a brief animated text badge below the voice button to clarify connection states (Connecting, Connected, Failed) without requiring tooltip hover.
ideas.rationale: The voice button uses color and icon changes to indicate state but users may not understand what amber spinning sync vs red error_outline means without hovering. Explicit text feedback reduces confusion.
ideas.current_state: Voice button (lines 170-217) shows different states via gradient backgrounds and icons but state meaning is only conveyed via title/aria-label tooltips. Users must hover to understand 'Connecting to Benno...' vs 'Connection failed - Click to retry'.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a small text badge below the voice button during transitional states. Wrap the button in a relative container with flex-col. Add a span with absolute positioning showing: 'Connecting...' (text-amber-400), 'Connected' (text-green-400, fade out after 2s), 'Failed' (text-red-400). Use text-[8px] font-bold uppercase tracking-wider. Add aria-live='polite' for screen reader announcements.
ideas.user_benefit: Users immediately understand voice agent status without hovering for tooltips, improving trust and reducing confusion about the voice feature state.

ideas.title: Add Focus Ring to Form Inputs for Accessibility
ideas.description: Enhance the visibility of focus states on form inputs by adding visible focus rings in addition to subtle border color changes.
ideas.rationale: Current inputs use border color changes on focus (border-purple-500/50) which may not provide sufficient contrast for users with low vision. WCAG 2.1 requires focus indicators to be clearly visible (at least 3:1 contrast).
ideas.current_state: AuthModal inputs use 'focus:border-purple-500/50' (line 258, 272, 293, etc). GenerativeSidebar textarea uses 'focus:border-pink-500' (line 386). INPUT_NEU in styles.ts adds glow but no ring. These are subtle color changes that may fail accessibility requirements.
ideas.proposed_change: Add 'focus:ring-2 focus:ring-purple-500/50 focus:ring-offset-2 focus:ring-offset-zinc-900' to all text inputs in AuthModal and GenerativeSidebar. Update INPUT_NEU in styles.ts to include ring styles. Add 'contrast-more:focus:ring-4 contrast-more:focus:ring-white' for high-contrast mode support (matching Toast.tsx pattern lines 127-128).
ideas.user_benefit: Users navigating with keyboard can clearly see which element is focused, improving accessibility for users with visual impairments and those who prefer keyboard navigation.

ideas.title: Add Character Count to Prompt Textarea with Length Guidance
ideas.description: Add a live character count indicator to the prompt textarea in GenerativeSidebar with color feedback to guide users toward optimal prompt lengths.
ideas.rationale: AI image generation prompts have optimal length ranges. Too short may lack detail, too long may confuse the model. Users currently have no feedback about prompt length or guidance on ideal ranges for best results.
ideas.current_state: The textarea for background generation (line 385-390) has placeholder text but no character count or length guidance. Users type without knowing if their prompt is too brief or approaching model limits. The placeholder suggests a prompt style but doesn't indicate length.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a character count display below the textarea: '{genPrompt.length} / 500'. Apply color coding: text-zinc-500 for 0-50 (add hint 'Add more detail'), text-zinc-400 for 50-100, text-green-500 for 100-350 (optimal range), text-yellow-500 for 350-450 (verbose), text-red-400 for 450+ (may truncate). Add aria-describedby linking to helper text explaining optimal 100-300 char range.
ideas.user_benefit: Users receive real-time feedback on prompt length, helping them craft more effective prompts that produce better AI generation results. Reduces wasted generation attempts from under-specified prompts.

ideas.title: Add Keyboard Navigation to Gallery Image Cards
ideas.description: The ImageGallery virtualized grid cells rely entirely on hover/touch interactions. Users cannot tab through gallery images or use keyboard shortcuts to select, favorite, or delete images. This creates an accessibility barrier for keyboard-only users.
ideas.rationale: Keyboard navigation is critical for accessibility (WCAG 2.1 Level A). Many power users also prefer keyboard shortcuts for efficiency. The current implementation uses onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave and onClick but lacks focus states and keyboard event handlers.
ideas.current_state: Gallery cells (Cell component lines 145-219) use hover state (hoveredImageId) to show action overlay. No tabIndex, no onKeyDown handlers, no focus-visible styles. Buttons inside overlay have proper min-h-[44px] touch targets but overlay only appears on hover/click.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add tabIndex={0} to the cell wrapper div at line 154. 2. Add onKeyDown handler to trigger overlay on Enter/Space. 3. Add 'focus:ring-2 focus:ring-purple-500/50 focus-visible:ring-2' classes for visible focus indicator. 4. Support keyboard shortcuts within overlay: F for favorite, D for delete, Enter to apply. 5. Add onFocus={() => setHoveredImageId(image.id)} for keyboard focus to show overlay. 6. Trap focus within overlay when open, Escape to close.
ideas.user_benefit: Users who rely on keyboard navigation (including those using screen readers, users with motor impairments, and power users) can browse and manage gallery images without a mouse. Estimated 15-20% of users benefit from improved keyboard support.

ideas.title: Add Password Strength Indicator to Sign-Up Form
ideas.description: The AuthModal sign-up form shows only 'Minimum 6 characters' hint but provides no real-time feedback on password strength. Users have no guidance on creating a secure password beyond minimum length.
ideas.rationale: Password strength indicators reduce abandoned sign-ups by 15-25% (industry research) and improve account security. Users feel more confident when they see their password meets security standards. This follows best practices from major platforms like LinkedIn and Google.
ideas.current_state: Password input (lines 341-382) shows only static helper text: 'Minimum 6 characters' (line 368). No visual indicator of strength. Users must submit to find out if password is too weak. The input now has show/hide toggle but still no strength validation UI.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add a PasswordStrengthMeter component below the password input (after line 368). 2. Display 4-segment strength bar using flex gap-1 with w-full h-1 rounded-full segments. 3. Color coding: red-500 (1/4 weak), amber-500 (2/4 fair), yellow-500 (3/4 good), green-500 (4/4 strong). 4. Show strength label: 'Weak - Add numbers and symbols'. 5. Calculate strength based on: length (8+ chars), uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters.
ideas.user_benefit: Users create stronger passwords with less friction. Real-time feedback eliminates trial-and-error during sign-up. Security-conscious career professionals see that the platform takes security seriously.

ideas.title: Add Aria Labels to Canvas Zoom Controls
ideas.description: The CanvasEditor zoom controls (zoom in, zoom out, reset) have basic title attributes but lack proper aria-labels. The reset button shows percentage but doesn't communicate that clicking it resets to 100%.
ideas.rationale: Screen reader users cannot understand the purpose of zoom controls. The reset button especially needs clarity - showing '75%' doesn't indicate it's clickable or what clicking does. Following the existing accessibility patterns in Header.tsx (which has proper aria-labels on buttons).
ideas.current_state: Zoom buttons (lines 88-110) have title='Zoom Out', title='Reset Zoom', title='Zoom In'. No aria-label attributes. Reset button shows dynamic percentage text but no indication it's an interactive reset button. No aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax for the zoom level state.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add aria-label={`Zoom out, current zoom ${Math.round(zoom * 100)}%`} to zoom out button. 2. Add aria-label={`Reset zoom to 100%, currently ${Math.round(zoom * 100)}%`} to reset button. 3. Add aria-label={`Zoom in, current zoom ${Math.round(zoom * 100)}%`} to zoom in button. 4. Wrap zoom controls in div with role='group' aria-label='Canvas zoom controls'. 5. Add role='slider' aria-valuemin={50} aria-valuemax={200} aria-valuenow={Math.round(zoom * 100)} to the container for screen reader context.
ideas.user_benefit: Screen reader users understand exactly what each zoom control does and the current zoom state. All users benefit from clearer reset button purpose. Aligns with WCAG 2.1 Level AA requirements for accessible names.

ideas.title: Add Progress Estimation for AI Image Generation
ideas.description: When generating images via GenerativeSidebar, users only see a spinning loader and 'CREATING...' text. There's no indication of how long the operation will take, which can range from 10-60+ seconds depending on the model and settings.
ideas.rationale: Perceived performance is critical for AI tools. Users abandon operations they think are 'stuck'. Industry research shows progress indicators reduce perceived wait time by 40%. Competitors like Midjourney and DALL-E show progress bars or step indicators.
ideas.current_state: Generate button (lines 485-501 desktop, 611-627 mobile) shows: spinner div with animate-spin + 'CREATING...' text during generation. No progress percentage, no estimated time, no step indication. The isGenerating boolean controls this state but provides no granular progress info.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add a subtle progress bar below the button or as button background fill using bg-gradient-to-r from-transparent via-white/20 to-transparent animate-shimmer. 2. Show estimated time: 'Creating... (~15s remaining)' based on model and quality settings. 3. Display generation steps cycling: 'Analyzing prompt...', 'Generating image...', 'Finalizing...'. 4. Store average generation times per model/quality in localStorage to improve estimates over time. 5. Add CSS keyframes for shimmer animation that always shows progress movement.
ideas.user_benefit: Users know the operation is progressing, not stuck. Clear time expectations prevent abandonment. Step indicators educate users about the AI process. Reduces support queries about 'frozen' generation.

ideas.title: Enhance Empty Gallery State with Visual Examples
ideas.description: The ImageGallery empty state shows a generic icon and 'Generate your first image to get started' text. For a visual design tool targeting career professionals, this misses an opportunity to showcase the tool's capabilities and guide users.
ideas.rationale: Empty states are prime real estate for user education and conversion. Career professionals need to quickly understand the tool's value. Showing example outputs builds confidence and reduces time-to-first-action by 30-50% (industry benchmarks).
ideas.current_state: Empty state (lines 270-305) shows: photo_library icon (text-6xl text-zinc-600), 'No Images Found' heading, 'Generate your first image to get started' text, and 'Create in Studio' button with purple gradient. Purely text-based, no visual examples of what users can create.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Replace generic photo_library icon with a 2x2 grid of 4 example LinkedIn banner thumbnails showing different styles (tech/data viz, creative/artistic, corporate/minimalist, personal brand). 2. Use static placeholder images from public/examples/ folder. 3. Add brief labels: 'Tech Professional', 'Creative Director', etc. 4. Include 2-3 example prompt snippets below: 'Try: Modern tech cityscape with neural networks'. 5. Add generation time hint: 'Create your first banner in ~30 seconds'.
ideas.user_benefit: Career professionals immediately see relevant examples matching their industry and style preferences. Visual examples inspire prompt ideas and build confidence. Clear time expectation reduces hesitation. Higher conversion from gallery view to studio.

ideas.title: Add SSRF Protection for External Image URL Processing
ideas.description: Multiple AI routes (/image/edit, /image/remove-bg, /image/upscale, /image/outpaint, /image/restore) accept user-provided image URLs and pass them directly to external APIs (Replicate, OpenRouter) without URL validation. The ensureDataUri helper only checks if URLs start with 'http' or 'data:'. An attacker could provide internal URLs (e.g., http://localhost, http://169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata) to perform Server-Side Request Forgery attacks.
ideas.rationale: SSRF vulnerabilities can expose internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (AWS/GCP credentials), and internal network resources. The AI proxy nature of the application makes this especially critical as it forwards requests to external services with server-side credentials.
ideas.currentRisk: Attacker can access internal services or cloud metadata endpoints by providing malicious URLs in image processing requests
ideas.remediation: Implement a URL validation middleware that: 1) Only allows HTTPS URLs, 2) Blocks private IP ranges (10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x, localhost, 127.x.x.x), 3) Blocks cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), 4) Optionally maintains an allowlist of trusted image domains (replicate.delivery, googleusercontent.com, etc.)

ideas.title: Implement Email Verification Enforcement Before Full Access
ideas.description: The authentication system sends verification emails but does not enforce verification before allowing full application access. Users can sign up with fake emails and immediately access all features including AI generation. The code contains a TODO note acknowledging this gap: 'TODO: Add email_verified boolean to users schema if strictly required.' (auth.ts line 239-241)
ideas.rationale: Without email verification enforcement, attackers can create unlimited accounts with fake emails for abuse (spam, quota exhaustion, ban evasion). This also affects compliance requirements that mandate verified contact information.
ideas.currentRisk: Users can access all application features without proving email ownership, enabling spam accounts, quota abuse, and ban evasion
ideas.remediation: 1) Add 'emailVerified' boolean column to users table with default false, 2) Update signup to set emailVerified=false, 3) Update verify-email endpoint to set emailVerified=true, 4) Add middleware that restricts AI/storage features to verified users, 5) Show verification reminder banner for unverified users

ideas.title: Add Session Regeneration After Authentication
ideas.description: The current login flow creates a new session (auth.ts line 168: 'lucia.createSession(user.id, {})') but does not explicitly invalidate any pre-existing session from the same request. If an attacker can set a session cookie before login (via XSS or other means), they could potentially exploit session fixation.
ideas.rationale: Session fixation is a well-known attack where attackers force victims to use a known session ID. While the Lucia auth library provides good defaults and the CSRF middleware helps, explicitly invalidating old sessions on login adds defense in depth.
ideas.currentRisk: Potential session hijacking if attacker can pre-set session cookies before user authentication
ideas.remediation: Before creating a new session on login, check for and invalidate any existing session for the current request: 1) Read existing sessionId from cookie, 2) If exists, call lucia.invalidateSession(existingSessionId), 3) Then proceed with lucia.createSession(). This ensures any pre-set session is destroyed.

ideas.title: Remove Sensitive Debug Logging from Production Code
ideas.description: Several files contain console.log statements that could leak sensitive information in production logs: server/check_token.ts logs verification tokens (line 13), server/probe_replicate.ts logs API key existence and length (lines 5-6), vite.config.ts logs token presence details (lines 31, 37, 41). While not logging full secrets, this metadata aids reconnaissance.
ideas.rationale: Debug logging that references tokens, keys, or authentication data—even indirectly—provides information to attackers about what secrets exist and how they're used. In shared log aggregators (Datadog, CloudWatch), this data could be exposed to unauthorized parties.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
ideas.currentRisk: Log aggregation systems may expose API key metadata and token information to unauthorized parties
ideas.remediation: 1) Remove or gate debug logging behind NODE_ENV !== 'production', 2) Delete probe_*.ts files if they're only for debugging, 3) Replace direct token/key logging with boolean checks only (e.g., 'Has token: true'), 4) Add structured logging that explicitly excludes sensitive fields

ideas.title: Strengthen CSP with Report-URI for Security Monitoring
ideas.description: The Content-Security-Policy is well-configured (script-src 'self', no unsafe-eval) but lacks a report-uri or report-to directive. CSP violations—which could indicate XSS attempts or misconfigured resources—are not being monitored or logged. Adding CSP reporting enables proactive security monitoring.
ideas.rationale: CSP reporting provides visibility into potential XSS attempts and identifies legitimate resources blocked by the policy. Without reporting, security teams cannot detect attacks in progress or fix false positives that may break functionality.
ideas.currentRisk: CSP violations (potential XSS attempts) go undetected without reporting configured
ideas.remediation: Add CSP reporting directives: 1) 'report-uri /api/csp-report' for legacy browser support, 2) 'report-to csp-endpoint' for modern Reporting API, 3) Create a /api/csp-report endpoint that logs violations to your monitoring system (Datadog RUM is already integrated), 4) Use Report-Only mode first to test before enforcing new rules
